binders: An arbitrary finite index type ι.
An arbitrary measurable sample space Ω.
A probability measure μ on Ω.
A family of Boolean-valued functions B_i:Ω→Bool indexed by i∈ι.
hypotheses: The index cardinality n=|ι| is strictly positive.
Every B_i is measurable into Bool with its discrete measurable structure.
The indexed family (B_i) is jointly independent under μ.
For every i, the pushforward distribution of B_i under μ is Bernoulli with success probability 1/2.
conclusions: Let S(ω)=∑_{i∈ι} 1_{B_i(ω)=true}. The event {ω:S(ω)≥3n/4} is exactly the event {ω:(S(ω)−n/2)/√(n/4)≥√(n/4)}.
mathematical_definitions: LocalDef001(b)=1 if b=true and LocalDef001(b)=0 otherwise.
LocalDef002 is the Bernoulli PMF on Bool with parameter 1/2, so true and false each have probability 1/2.
The number n is the finite cardinality |ι|, cast to Real inside the formulas.
The square root is the nonnegative real square root.
Both comparisons are nonstrict ≥ comparisons, so equality at the threshold is included.
translation.proposition_plain_english: For a nonempty finite family of jointly independent fair Boolean random variables, encode true as 1 and false as 0 and let S be their sum. The outcomes for which S is at least three quarters of the number of variables are exactly the outcomes for which the centered and scaled quantity (S−n/2)/√(n/4) is at least √(n/4).

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: The strict positivity of n ensures n/4>0 and therefore √(n/4)>0, so the standardizing denominator is nonzero.
The conclusion is equality of sets of outcomes, not merely equality of their probabilities.
The identity is one-sided: the standardized expression is not inside an absolute value.
All thresholds are real numbers; no integer rounding is performed.
Measurability, independence, the probability-measure assumption, and the fair marginal laws are included hypotheses but are not needed for the pointwise algebraic set identity itself.
The hypotheses are satisfiable for standard finite products of fair Boolean variables, so the proposition is not vacuous.
